1.explanation:
1. MultiSelect.js: This is the core component. We need to introduce and honor a new readOnly prop, apply a ‘read-only’ class (to match the design), and guard all interactive behavior (prevent opening the menu, block deselect/select events, render the tag count view).  
2. MultiSelectPropTypes.js: We must add the readOnly prop to the component’s PropTypes so consumers get validation and documentation of the new API.  
3. MultiSelect.stories.js: To meet the “Controls for each state” and “Default story” criteria, we need to add readOnly to the story argTypes, include it in the Playground control panel, and ship a default story showcasing read-only mode for easy copy/paste.  
4. __tests__/MultiSelect-test.js: We need to add RTL tests verifying that when readOnly=true, the component renders the correct class, does not open on click or keyboard events, and still displays the selected count tag correctly, satisfying the requirement for RTL tests on the read-only class.
1.bug_scenario: The provided images outline the visual design and layout for a read-only version of the MultiSelect dropdown. The first diagram (“Structure”) shows two states: an empty read-only input (with placeholder text “Choose options…”) and a filled read-only input (showing a tag with a count badge “2 ×” that can’t be removed). It also annotates consistent spacing (16px margins, 24px height, 10px tag radius, 1px borders). The second diagram (“Color and typography”) specifies the color tokens for text (e.g. $text-secondary, $text-placeholder), disabled icon color ($icon-disabled), transparent background, border color ($border-strong-01), and helper text color. It also shows the filled state—primary text color for the “2 filters are selected” label—and the tag’s styling in that state.
